slides.title: Seeing Touch from Motion: A Unified Modality-Aware Visuo-Tactile Policy with Tactile Motion Correlation
slides.tldr: NEW VISUO-TACTILE POLICY FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a motion-aware tactile representation and a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture to better distinguish fine-grained contact states and fuse visual and tactile modalities.

card.one_liner: A visuo-tactile policy using motion-aware tactile representations and a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture for contact-rich manipulation.
card.key_idea: Combines transient and cumulative tactile motion correlations to distinguish fine-grained contact states, fused via a Mixture-of-Transformers to balance cross-modal interaction and modality-specific properties.

slides.title: TAP-VLA: Tactile Annotation Prompting for Vision Language Action Models
slides.tldr: TACTILE FEEDBACK VIA VISUAL AUGMENTATION FOR VLAs
slides.highlight: TAP-VLA integrates tactile sensing into Vision-Language-Action models by overlaying shear fields as vectors on RGB images, avoiding architectural changes and distribution shifts. This approach significantly improves success rates in contact-rich manipulation tasks compared to vision-only or tactile-fusion baselines.

card.one_liner: TAP-VLA integrates tactile feedback into pre-trained VLAs by rendering tactile shear fields as visual annotations.
card.key_idea: Extracts shear fields from visuo-tactile sensors and overlays them as spatially-grounded vectors onto RGB images, avoiding architectural changes and distribution shifts from new modalities.
card.evaluation: Tested on four contact-rich tasks; TAP-VLA achieved 78% success rate, significantly outperforming vision-only and tactile-fusion baselines (all <50%).
card.limitation: Downsampling discards detailed grasp geometry, and annotations may occlude task-relevant visual content in cluttered scenes.

slides.authors: Mark Van der Merwe et al.

slides.title: VibeAct: Vibration to Actions for Contact-Rich Reactive Robot Dexterity
slides.highlight: VibeAct uses piezoelectric microphones to bridge real vibrotactile sensing with simulation-based reinforcement learning via a shared representation of contact and slip. This approach improves success rates in contact-rich tasks like regrasping and insertion by providing rapid tactile feedback.

card.one_liner: VibeAct enables sim-to-real dexterous manipulation by bridging vibrotactile sensing and RL via a shared contact-slip representation.
card.key_idea: A tactile estimator maps real microphone signals to a compact contact/slip representation, which is also computed directly in simulation to train RL policies.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five contact-rich tasks using PPO; outperformed proprioception+point-cloud baselines in simulation and improved success rates on physical hardware deployment.
card.limitation: Discards raw vibration details (e.g., texture), depends on accurate object pose tracking for labeling, and requires recalibration for hardware changes.

slides.title: PhysReflect-VLA: Physical Feasibility and Self-Reflective Regulation for Reliable Vision-Language-Action Policies
slides.tldr: SELF-REFLECTIVE VLA FRAMEWORK FOR ROBOTIC MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that uses physical feasibility evaluation and an LLM-based reflection module to diagnose execution errors and generate corrective guidance. It is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring, self-correction via meta-cognition, and adaptive agent behavior.

card.one_liner: PhysReflect-VLA enhances VLA policies with real-time physical feasibility checks and self-reflective error correction for robotic manipulation.
card.key_idea: A plug-and-play framework using a bidirectional consistency model (forward/inverse operators) to filter infeasible actions and an LLM-based module to generate corrective guidance from execution discrepancies.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks; outperformed baselines like OpenVLA with an average success rate gain of 5.4%.

slides.title: Bridging Handheld and Teleoperated Supervision for Contact-Rich Manipulation via State-Gated Experts
slides.tldr: HYBRID DATA COLLECTION FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: The BRIDGE framework combines scalable handheld data with targeted teleoperated demonstrations using a mixture of diffusion policy experts to improve success rates in contact-sensitive tasks.

card.one_liner: BRIDGE improves contact-rich manipulation by routing between handheld-observed and teleoperated-desired action experts based on robot state.
card.key_idea: A mixture-of-diffusion-experts architecture using a state-conditioned MLP router to switch between a base policy (handheld data) and a support head (targeted teleoperation).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three contact-rich tasks (pulley routing, pipe insertion, battery insertion) against handheld-only and naive-mix baselines; success rates increased by up to 36.7%.
card.limitation: Hard-switching causes control discontinuities; identifying support regions is currently empirical; may scale poorly to long-horizon tasks with many contact regimes.

slides.title: ForesightSafety-VLA: A Unified Diagnostic Safety Benchmark for Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.tldr: DIAGNOSTIC SAFETY BENCHMARK FOR VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a safety benchmark for vision-language-action models, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A diagnostic benchmark for VLA models evaluating embodied safety across physical, linguistic, and perceptual dimensions.
card.key_idea: A 13-category safety taxonomy using 66 RoboTwin scenarios, measuring process-level risk via cumulative safety cost (CC) and risk exposure time (RET) across three controlled variation dimensions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated representative VLA baselines (e.g., OpenVLA-oft, RDT, ACT) using a four-quadrant outcome decomposition. Results show pervasive unsafe behavior and high sensitivity to visual/structural changes.
card.limitation: The current release is limited to simulated tabletop manipulation and lacks real-world validation or mobile manipulation scenarios.

slides.title: OpenSPM: An Environment-Transferable Robotic Key Spatial Pose Memory and Closed-Loop High-Frequency Flow-Matching Action Generation Model
slides.tldr: HIGH-FREQUENCY ACTION GENERATION VIA SPATIAL POSE MEMORY
slides.highlight: OpenSPM introduces a spatial persistent memory framework that combines 6D pose tracking with a conditional flow-matching model to achieve high-frequency robotic manipulation. The system enables environment-transferable action generation with a reported 85.6% success rate across ten LIBERO-GOAL tasks.

card.one_liner: OpenSPM enables high-frequency, environment-transferable robotic manipulation using object-centric spatial pose memory and flow-matching action generation.
card.key_idea: Decomposes manipulation into semantic 3D perception, retrieval of relative key spatial poses from a memory bank, SE(3) transfer, and lightweight conditional flow-matching for action chunks.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on ten LIBERO-GOAL tasks; achieved 85.6% success rate and 1033.3 Hz equivalent frequency, outperforming VLA and diffusion baselines.
card.limitation: Performance depends on initial segmentation/reconstruction quality; struggles with occlusions, visually similar objects, and narrow operation tolerances.

slides.title: Behavior Uncloning: Distilling Mode Redirection into Policy Weights without Inference-Time Steering
slides.tldr: DISTILLING MODE REDIRECTION TO SUPPRESS UNDESIRED BEHAVIORS
slides.highlight: This work introduces MoRE to redirect policy rollouts toward desired behavior modes, supporting the MOSAIC goal of aligning human-AI intent by suppressing unsafe or undesired modes without inference-time overhead.

card.one_liner: MoRE distills mode-redirection signals into policy weights to suppress undesired behaviors without inference-time overhead.
card.key_idea: A temporary mode classifier provides a differentiable redirection loss to update policy weights, balanced by a retain loss to preserve task competence and a source-mode probability mask.
card.evaluation: Tested on 8 simulated and real-world tasks using Diffusion Policy and $\pi_{0.5}$ VLA; improved average success rate by 44 percentage points over original policies.
card.limitation: Requires mode-labeled editing data and a classifier interface that exposes mode information before trajectories commit to a specific mode.
